source_pose.coordinate_note: Follow the curved source sweep for local orientation; -x is the authored overall heartward direction.

native_application_path.application: Merge function_view_notes.json notes into lead teaching camera records and present sequences in companion guide. Preserve camera geometry, hidden-part partitions, assembled state and cut settings from teaching specialist.
native_application_path.runtime_effect: Static camera/visibility changes only. Sequence prose is a guide/archival field, not an animation or simulated flow field.
native_application_path.prohibited_inference: No arbitrary physiological states, pressure values or streamlines are applied to the mesh.

functional_sequences.mechanism: A supported intimal fold provides a direction-sensitive valve while the sinus remains continuous with the lumen.

steps.anatomical_function: Trace lining into each cusp, distinguish attached U-shaped root from free margin, and identify the sinus behind the leaflet. Heartward is -x, decreasing sweep station. Pocket mouths face the heartward/downstream side.
Hide the endothelial covering to reveal its supporting core in the same location, then restore the covering. This is an explanatory reveal, not removal of tissue in life.

In living forward flow, opening moves cusps toward the sinus wall. Sinus recirculation can exchange pocket blood with the main stream. The displayed near-closed pose stays unchanged; it does not visualize that cycle.

schematic_limitations: Neither the narrow inter-cusp corridor nor either rear pocket is certified patent by source formulas or visibility.
No arrows, tracer particles, fluid solution, leaflet timing, pressure field or valve motion are supplied.
Sinus pocket location does not establish stasis, trapped blood or thrombosis.
The 2003 primary abstract was retrieved through NLM search; direct page content retrieval failed, so its full text and figures were not inspected.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Valve topology is oriented to oppose retrograde return; normal closure need not wait for through-valve reverse flow.

steps.anatomical_function: Identify the downstream-facing pocket mouths. A reversed pressure difference can load the pocket sides and favor approximation of the free margins; this is a qualitative mechanism, not a tested state of this mesh.
Physiological ultrasound observed closure associated with flow deceleration and changing sinus shape without requiring through-valve backflow. Do not teach reverse flow as a mandatory first step.
The source keeps a nearly closed teaching pose with a small apparent slit. Do not diagnose competence, reflux, obstruction or disease from this static shape.

schematic_limitations: No pressure-loaded coaptation, leak test, reflux duration or flow resistance was computed.
A numerical nonzero corridor, if later established, remains a geometric result rather than physiological valve competence.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Venous geometry and smooth-muscle tone contribute to the blood-volume reservoir.

steps.anatomical_function: Compare the broad lumen, relatively thin media and supporting adventitia. These are representative venous relationships; no same-caliber arterial comparison or patient measurement is present.

Capacitance means contained volume at a given distending pressure; compliance means the change in volume for a change in pressure. A thin, deformable wall illustrates the concept, not a measured pressure-volume relation.

Venous smooth-muscle contraction can reduce capacitance and recruit unstressed into stressed volume. Regional reservoirs, especially the splanchnic bed, govern the whole-system effect; this small valved segment does not quantify it.

schematic_limitations: No wall distension, collapse, venoconstriction or pressure-volume curve is animated.
Whole-system venous blood-volume fractions are context, not a volume encoded by these enlarged cells.
Do not equate capacitance with compliance or guarantee that local constriction always increases venous return.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Connective tissue integrates muscular, vascular, neural and adipose elements around the thin-walled vein.

steps.anatomical_function: Keep the adventitial carrier present while identifying collagen and longitudinal muscle samples. The outer connective transition supports and anchors the vein; it is not a detached casing.

Follow longitudinal bundle orientation and contrast it with circumferential media muscle. Prominent longitudinal adventitial muscle varies by venous region; the six draft representatives are teaching samples, not a physiological count.
Relate enlarged adipocyte samples to the adventitial connective environment and restore the whole specimen. Do not infer perivascular inflammatory or endocrine activity from the static outer fat.

schematic_limitations: This is a representative valved medium-vein teaching composite, not the vena cava or a universal venous wall.
No collagen recruitment, wall tension, suture holding or adipokine assay is measured.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Wall microvessels nourish tissue; autonomic innervation modulates vascular smooth-muscle tone.

steps.anatomical_function: Follow enlarged Vasa vasorum representatives into and beside the adventitia. They represent wall supply, distinct from blood in the vein main lumen.

Real wall circulation includes exchange microvessels and venous drainers. The named red Vasa vasorum part lacks a separately displayed complete capillary and venous drainage circuit; cut ends mark a cropped specimen, not demonstrated closed-loop perfusion.

Relate the nervi vasorum to vascular muscle in the supporting environment. Sympathetic signaling is a narrated biological connection; proximity of a colored strand does not verify a terminal or demonstrate contraction.

schematic_limitations: The human great-saphenous-vein study provides a specific anatomical example, not a required spacing/depth for this composite.
Do not assert the red vessel graph is universally arterial or has demonstrated supply and drainage.
No lumen/perfusion certification, oxygen gradient, neurotransmitter diffusion, receptor response or neural firing is supplied.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Sparse enlarged blood-cell examples provide context; recruitment is a distinct dynamic and molecular process.

steps.anatomical_function: Red cells and the leukocyte are sparse enlarged symbols. They do not specify hematocrit, cell count, occlusion or sinus residence time.

Inspect the leukocyte example near the endothelial lining. Retain the stable part key Rolling leukocyte but caption it as a static cell example; rolling, firm adhesion and transmigration are not demonstrated by a stationary sphere.

For context, selectin-mediated tethering and rolling cooperate with activation and integrin-dependent firm adhesion before tissue entry. Recruitment is chiefly a postcapillary-venule lesson, not a process established in every valved vein.

schematic_limitations: No selectins, integrins, chemokines, endothelial junctions or tracked cell displacement are modeled.
The 1998 functional experiment studied TNF-treated mouse cremaster venules; it does not establish recruitment in this representative medium vein.
Neutrophil identity is not demonstrated by external lumpiness alone.
